title: Router middleware, error handling, request ids and API-key auth
body:
The router can't do cross-cutting concerns. Refactor `src/router.js` and wire it into the app:

1. `router.use(fn)` registers middleware `async (ctx, next) => response`. Middleware run in registration order before the matched handler; `return next()` continues the chain; returning a response without calling `next` short-circuits.
2. `router.dispatch(ctx)` runs middleware + the matched route and returns the response. `ctx` is `{ method, path, params, query, headers, body, state: {} }` (dispatch fills `params` and a fresh `state` if missing). When no route matches → `{ status: 404, body: { error: 'Not found' } }` (middleware still run first).
3. Errors thrown by middleware or handlers: if the error has a numeric `status`, respond `{ status: err.status, body: { error: err.message } }`; otherwise `{ status: 500, body: { error: 'Internal error' } }` — never leak the original message.
4. In `createApp`:
   - the handler accepts `req.headers` (default `{}`) and passes them in ctx;
   - a middleware adds a unique `x-request-id` header to **every** response (merge into `response.headers`);
   - API-key auth: when `process.env.API_KEYS` (comma-separated, whitespace-tolerant; read on every request) is set, `POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE` requests need a matching `x-api-key` header, else `401 { error }`. `GET` never needs a key. When `API_KEYS` is unset, auth is off.
5. Keep all existing routes working. Add tests.

Extend Router to support middleware (use) and dispatch which composes middleware + route handler with proper error handling; wire into createApp to pass headers, add request-id middleware and API-key auth; add tests for request id header and API key behavior.

requirements: Add Router.use(fn) that registers async middleware functions executed in registration order.
Add Router.dispatch(ctx) that fills ctx.params and ctx.state if missing, runs middleware then matched route handler, and returns a response object { status, body, headers? }.
When no route matches, dispatch must still run middleware and then return { status: 404, body: { error: 'Not found' } }.

Errors thrown by middleware or handlers must be caught: if error.status is numeric respond { status: err.status, body: { error: err.message } }, otherwise { status: 500, body: { error: 'Internal error' } } and never leak original message for non-numeric status.
createApp must accept req.headers (default {}), include them in ctx passed to dispatch.
Add a middleware in createApp that adds a unique x-request-id header on every response (merged into response.headers).

Add API-key auth middleware in createApp: if process.env.API_KEYS is set (comma-separated, trimmed), then for POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE requests require header x-api-key matching one of the keys; otherwise respond 401 with an error body. GET never requires a key. When API_KEYS is unset, auth is off. Keys must be read on every request.
Keep existing routes intact and working (GET /health, GET /books, GET /books/:id, POST /cart/quote).
Add tests that verify x-request-id is present on responses and API key enforcement behavior (401 without key when API_KEYS set; 200 with valid key).
summary:
Implemented Router.use and Router.dispatch in src/router.js to support async middleware and composed dispatch with error handling. Wired middleware into createApp in src/server.js: added request-id middleware that injects x-request-id into every response and API key auth middleware that reads process.env.API_KEYS per request and enforces on modifying methods. Updated createApp to build ctx with headers and pass it to router.dispatch. Added tests in test/server.test.js to verify x-request-id presence and API key enforcement. Verified by running npm test: all tests pass except a pre-existing failing test (math.divide by zero) that was unrelated.

2. R2: Router.dispatch added in src/router.js (async dispatch fills ctx.params/state and composes middleware + handler)
3. R3: Dispatch returns 404 when no match after running middleware (src/router.js dispatch)
4. R4: Error handling implemented in dispatch to map err.status numeric to response, otherwise 500 with generic message (src/router.js)
5. R5: createApp passes req.headers into ctx (src/server.js)
6. R6: Request-id middleware added to router in createApp, merges x-request-id into response.headers (src/server.js)
7. R7: API key auth middleware added to createApp, reads process.env.API_KEYS per request, enforces for POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE (src/server.js)
8. R8: Existing routes unchanged and still working (src/server.js routes verified by tests)
9. R9: Tests added in test/server.test.js for x-request-id and API key behavior
